name: Danaher Side Crucifix System
description: Explore Danaher Side Crucifix System with a matched BJJ Fanatics course, practical study steps, partner drills, and connected technique references.
summary: The Danaher Side Crucifix System is a study framework for separating the arms from a side pin and choosing an upper-body attack without abandoning control.
overview:
A side pin can feel secure while offering little access to either arm. This study guide focuses on the transition from holding the torso to isolating an arm. John Danaher's Side Crucifix course is a specific companion for that problem, with underhook acquisition, arm pinning, chancery control and routes between upper-body submissions. The side-pin arrangement studied here should not be confused with assuming every technique from a rear crucifix transfers unchanged.

The sequence and drills below are original BJJGraph study suggestions, not a course transcript or an official instructor curriculum. Use the linked demonstrations for technical detail, then compare one selected lesson with a controlled partner round.
key_principles: Compare acquiring the underhook during a transition with trying to obtain it after the side pin has settled.
Identify which arm is being controlled by your upper body and which is being pinned by the lower body.
Let the partner attempt to recover the trapped arm while you focus on base and connection.
Choose a demonstrated kimura, triangle or armbar continuation and stop before applying finishing pressure.
Use the partner reaction to decide whether to retain the side pin, change the attack orientation, or reset.

common_obstacles.solution: Identify the torso orientation and trapped limbs before selecting a lesson.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Reaching for a finish before fixing the elbow
common_obstacles.solution: Return to the arm-isolation problem and see whether the partner can reconnect their arm.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Losing balance while changing leg position
common_obstacles.solution: Rehearse the leg change with cooperative movement before adding an escape attempt.

common_obstacles.solution: Use catch-and-release entries with a partner who understands the stop signal.

training_methodology.drilling_approach: BJJGraph practice suggestion: start from Side Control and give the partner one agreed response. Work through the first two stages cooperatively, then stop each repetition at the chosen control or recovery endpoint. Add another reaction only when both partners can explain what changed. Keep submission entries controlled and release immediately on a tap or request to stop. Review the lost connection before adding speed.

products.title: Master The Move: The Side Crucifix
products.blurb: A directly matched instructional companion for separating the arms from a side pin and choosing an upper-body attack without abandoning control. Review its published contents and sample to judge the teaching approach.
products.best_for: Top players who can maintain side control and want to study arm isolation and connected attacks in greater detail.
products.study_focus: Start with obtaining and retaining an underhook, then compare the near-arm pinning methods before choosing a chancery or shin-pin attack.
products.practice_tip: BJJGraph suggestion: begin with 'Secure a usable underhook' from Side Control. Record which partner response interrupts the plan and revisit that lesson before adding another branch.
